NY LLC TRANSPARENCY ACT TRACKER · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER

Does your NY LLC owe a filing — and when?

Answer four questions to see your likely category and deadline under New York's LLC Transparency Act, then organize the beneficial-owner details you'll need before you file. This is not legal advice and not a determination of your actual filing status — see the disclaimer below before you rely on it.

Evidence and organizing only — you remain the filer. This tool applies your own answers to New York Department of State (NYDOS) guidance confirmed as of December 31, 2025. It never files anything, never contacts New York State, and never determines your LLC's actual legal status. Confirm your category and deadline directly with NYDOS or your own attorney before you rely on them.

1. Your likely category and deadline

Applicable initial deadline
Days remaining

Every LLC subject to the Act, reporting or exempt, also owes a recurring annual statement in later years confirming or updating its beneficial ownership information (or exempt status) — confirm your own annual due date directly with NYDOS.

2. Beneficial owner worksheet

Needed if your category looks like a Reporting Company. Nothing here is uploaded or sent anywhere — see the privacy note in the footer, including how the "keep this in my browser" option below works.

3. Download your organizer

This produces a draft document only. It does not file anything or contact New York State — review it, then email your own completed filing to NYDOS yourself.


  


  

    
Common questions

    
Who actually has to file under the NY LLC Transparency Act?

    
Per NYDOS guidance confirmed December 31, 2025, the reporting obligation (a full Beneficial Ownership Disclosure) applies only to an LLC formed outside the United States that is also formed in New York or authorized to transact business in New York. Every other LLC with a New York nexus — including an LLC formed in New York itself — is instead an "Exempt Company" that still must file an Attestation of Exemption. An LLC with no New York nexus at all is outside the Act's scope.

    
When is the deadline?

    
An LLC that already had a New York nexus before January 1, 2026 must file its initial disclosure or attestation by December 31, 2026. An LLC formed in New York, or authorized/registered to transact business in New York, on or after January 1, 2026 must file within 30 days of that formation or registration date. Every LLC subject to the Act also owes a recurring annual statement in later years.

    
How do I actually file?

    
As of this tool's last check, NYDOS had not yet launched an online filing portal — completed disclosures and exemption attestations, with the statutory filing fee, are submitted by email to doscorpboi@dos.ny.gov (case-insensitive). Confirm the current filing process directly with NYDOS before you send anything, since this can change once a portal launches.

    
Is this legal advice, or does it file anything for me?

    
No, to both. This tool applies the rule above to the answers you type and shows you the result — it does not know the full facts of your LLC's formation, does not model every exemption category NYDOS recognizes, and the statute and guidance can be amended. It never contacts New York State and never submits anything on your behalf; the organizer it produces is a draft for you to review and file yourself.

    
Is anything I type uploaded anywhere?

    
No. Every answer, and the entire beneficial-owner worksheet, is processed and rendered entirely in your browser from a fixed set of rules shipped with this page. Nothing is sent to a server. The worksheet is kept only in this browser's page memory unless you explicitly check "keep this in my browser" — see the privacy note in the footer.

  


  

    
No warranty. This tool is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. It is not legal, tax, or financial advice, and it does not replace a qualified attorney licensed in New York. It applies your own answers to a fixed reading of the NY LLC Transparency Act and NYDOS's confirmed guidance — nothing more — and does not model every exemption category, amendment, or fact pattern. You are responsible for reviewing and verifying its output before relying on it, and for meeting any filing obligation it helps you prepare for. To the maximum extent permitted by law, the authors accept no liability for any loss or damage arising from its use.

    
Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. We do not promise uptime, backups of anything you type, or that a URL will keep working. Do not use this as a system of record for a beneficial-owner worksheet — download your organizer and keep your own copy.

    
Everything runs in your browser. Nothing you type is ever uploaded; there are no accounts, tracking cookies, or analytics vendors. The beneficial-owner worksheet lives only in this page's memory and is lost on reload unless you check "keep this in my browser" above, which stores it in this device's local storage and nowhere else. Anonymous feature events (category_checked, owner_added, organizer_downloaded, csv_downloaded, example_loaded) are counted only in local storage and never include what you typed. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control are honoured.

    

    
Further reading: when is the NY LLC Transparency Act deadline, and how is it different from the federal Corporate Transparency Act?

    
Weighing this against the usual approach? This tracker vs. piecing it together from law-firm client alerts — including where a stale alert misstates who has to file, and when an attorney is still the right answer.

    
Tracking a different deadline? The grant deadline tracker covers nonprofit funder reporting dates instead of a state filing obligation.

    
Checking the separate federal filing instead? The BOI reporting exemption checker covers whether your entity still owes FinCEN a beneficial ownership report after the August 2026 final rule — a different agency, different scope, and (for most U.S.-formed entities) now a permanent exemption rather than a filing.

    
Free and open source. If this saved you a filing headache, the code is under an MIT licence — support is entirely optional and never changes what the tool does.

← Back to the NY LLC Transparency Act Tracker

This tracker vs. piecing it together from law-firm client alerts

This names no specific firm or product. It compares a free browser tool against the generic method most New York LLC owners actually use right now: searching the Act, landing on two or three law-firm client alerts, and assembling your own answer from them.

QuestionReading client alertsThis tracker
Which category your LLC is in The rule is explained in general; you apply it to your own facts You answer three questions — formed in New York, authorized in New York, formed outside the US — and it applies the published rule to those answers
Whether the scope narrowing is reflected Depends entirely on the alert's date. One written before the NYDOS guidance confirmed December 31, 2025 can describe a broader set of LLCs as Reporting Companies than current guidance does Applies the narrowed scope — a full Beneficial Ownership Disclosure only for an LLC formed outside the United States with a New York nexus — and says which guidance and date that comes from
Your own filing date Both deadline tracks are described; you work out which one you are on and count the days Computes the applicable initial deadline from your nexus date and shows a countdown to it
What to collect before filing Listed in prose, often mid-article, and you rebuild it as your own checklist Structured worksheet rows, plus a downloadable organizer and CSV to review before you write the filing email
Not confusing this with the federal filing Many alerts cover both the federal Corporate Transparency Act and the New York Act, which is thorough but easy to conflate on a skim Covers the New York state filing only, and says plainly that a FinCEN filing does not satisfy it
Authority behind the answer Its real strength — written and reviewed by licensed attorneys, and citable A likely category, not a determination. Not legal advice, and no substitute for counsel on a hard question
Where the beneficial-owner details live Usually a document or spreadsheet you create, syncing to whatever cloud account and sharing that folder already has In page memory only. No upload, no copy-a-link feature at all, and saving to your browser is off by default
Submitting the filing Explains the process; you send the email Never contacts New York State and files nothing — you remain the filer and send it yourself

Neither approach decides whether your LLC has a New York nexus, and neither files anything for you. Both are only as good as the facts you bring to them, and both should be checked against NYDOS before you rely on a date.

Common questions

Why not just read a law-firm client alert?

Client alerts are written by licensed attorneys and are usually accurate about the rule as of their publication date — that is their real strength, and this tool does not replace it. The friction is that an alert explains the rule in general while you still have to apply it to your own LLC, compute your own date, and build your own list of what to collect. The specific risk is date drift: NYDOS narrowed the reporting scope in guidance confirmed December 31, 2025, so an alert written before that change, or a search result surfacing one, can describe a broader set of LLCs as Reporting Companies than the current guidance does.

Does this tracker replace a lawyer?

No, and it is not trying to. This tool is a reference and an organizer: it applies a published rule to the facts you enter and arranges what you will need, but it produces a likely category rather than a determination of your actual filing status. It is not legal advice and does not replace an attorney licensed in New York. If your ownership structure is layered, contested, or you are unsure whether your LLC has a New York nexus at all, that is a question for counsel, not for a web page.

Is my beneficial-owner information safer here than in a shared document?

It is handled differently, and deliberately so. Beneficial-owner details are name, address, date of birth, and government ID number. This tool runs entirely in your browser, never uploads anything, ships no copy-a-link feature at all, and does not save the worksheet to your browser unless you explicitly switch that on — it is off by default, and reloading the page clears the worksheet. A document in a shared drive, by contrast, syncs to a cloud account and inherits whatever sharing that folder already has. Neither approach is a substitute for your own judgment about where this category of data belongs.

No warranty. This page is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. It is not legal advice, and it does not replace a qualified attorney licensed in New York. Statutes and agency guidance are amended without notice — verify the current rule directly with NYDOS before you rely on any date here.

Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice.

Use the NY LLC Transparency Act Tracker to check your own category and deadline, or read when is the NY LLC Transparency Act deadline? for the dates and how the New York filing differs from the federal one.

when-is-the-ny-llc-transparency-act-dead.text:
← Back to the NY LLC Transparency Act Tracker

When is the NY LLC Transparency Act deadline?

New York's LLC Transparency Act (Senate Bill 8059, signed March 1, 2024) took effect January 1, 2026. Its deadlines run on two tracks depending on when your LLC's New York nexus began.

What is the initial filing deadline?

An LLC whose New York nexus began before January 1, 2026 must file its initial disclosure or attestation by December 31, 2026. An LLC whose New York nexus began on or after January 1, 2026 must file within 30 days of that formation or registration date.

When the NY nexus beganInitial deadline
Before January 1, 2026December 31, 2026
On or after January 1, 202630 days from the formation/registration date

"New York nexus" means the LLC was formed under New York law, or is authorized/registered to transact business in New York as a foreign LLC. An LLC with neither is outside the Act's scope entirely.

Is there a recurring deadline after the initial filing?

Yes. Every LLC subject to the Act, whether a Reporting Company or an Exempt Company, must also file an annual statement confirming or updating its beneficial ownership information (or exempt status) and its principal executive office address. Confirm your own annual due date directly with the NY Department of State (NYDOS) — this tool computes only the initial deadline.

Who is a Reporting Company, and who is an Exempt Company?

Per NYDOS guidance confirmed December 31, 2025, the reporting obligation — a full Beneficial Ownership Disclosure naming each beneficial owner — applies only to an LLC formed outside the United States that also has a New York nexus. Every other LLC with a New York nexus, including one formed in New York itself, is instead an Exempt Company: it still must file, but as an Attestation of Exemption rather than a full disclosure.

How is this different from the federal Corporate Transparency Act?

They are two separate filings with two separate agencies. The federal Corporate Transparency Act is administered by FinCEN; New York's LLC Transparency Act is administered by the NY Department of State. Both ask about beneficial ownership, but a filing made under one does not satisfy the other, and their scope, exemptions, and deadlines are not identical. This tool covers only the New York state filing.

How do I actually submit a filing?

As of this tool's last check, NYDOS had not yet launched an online filing portal. Completed disclosures and exemption attestations, along with the statutory filing fee (by credit or debit card authorization), are submitted by email to doscorpboi@dos.ny.gov (case-insensitive). Confirm the current process directly with NYDOS before sending anything, since this can change once an online portal launches. This tool's organizer is a draft to review and attach — it does not send anything for you.

No warranty. This page is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. It is not legal advice, and it does not replace a qualified attorney licensed in New York. Statutes and agency guidance are amended without notice — verify the current rule directly with NYDOS before you rely on any date here.

Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice.
